records.context: **A cell is a set of objects.** :func:`cell_rows` is the whole primitive: the rows of the out-of-fold prediction table whose true class is *this* and whose predicted class is *that*. Everything else here is a way of ordering, splitting or counting that set.
records.label: spacr.confusion#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A cell is a set of objects.** :func:`cell_rows` is the whole primitive: the rows of the out-of-fold prediction table whose true class is *this* and whose predicted class is *that*. Everything else here is a way of ordering, splitting or counting that set.
records.translation: **Une cellule est un ensemble d’objets.** :func:`cell_rows` constitue à elle seule la primitive : les lignes de la table de prédictions hors pli dont la classe réelle est *celle-ci* et dont la classe prédite est *celle-là*. Tout le reste ici n’est qu’une manière d’ordonner, de répartir ou de compter cet ensemble.

records.source: **A confident error and an unsure error have different causes.** They are therefore two lists, never one sorted list with a gradient in it:
records.translation: **Une erreur confiante et une erreur incertaine ont des causes différentes.** Ce sont donc deux listes, jamais une seule liste triée comportant un gradient :

records.context: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the extracted image regions to re-label.

records.source: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the crops to re-label.
records.translation: **confiance élevée, et erreur** — le modèle était sûr de lui. Lorsqu’un modèle qui a raison 95% du temps est *certain* à propos d’un objet et contredit l’annotation, l’explication la plus probable est que l’annotation est fausse. Ce sont les rognages à réétiqueter.

records.context: ``confidence`` is the probability of the class the model *chose*, so it can never fall below ``1 / n_classes`` — a two-class model is at 0.5 when it is maximally undecided, and a ten-class model is at 0.1. A fixed 0.5 would therefore call every ten-class error "high confidence" and every two-class error nothing at all, which is the sort of default that makes a feature look broken on somebody else's data.
records.label: spacr.confusion.confidence_threshold#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``confidence`` is the probability of the class the model *chose*, so it can never fall below ``1 / n_classes`` — a two-class model is at 0.5 when it is maximally undecided, and a ten-class model is at 0.1. A fixed 0.5 would therefore call every ten-class error "high confidence" and every two-class error nothing at all, which is the sort of default that makes a feature look broken on somebody else's data.
records.translation: ``confidence`` est la probabilité de la classe que le modèle a *choisie* ; elle ne peut donc jamais descendre sous ``1 / n_classes`` — un modèle à deux classes est à 0.5 lorsqu’il est au maximum de l’indécision, et un modèle à dix classes est à 0.1. Un seuil fixe de 0.5 qualifierait donc chaque erreur à dix classes de "high confidence" et aucune erreur à deux classes, ce qui est le genre de valeur par défaut qui fait paraître une fonctionnalité cassée sur les données de quelqu’un d’autre.

records.context: The default is the midpoint between chance and certainty: 0.75 for two classes, 0.55 for ten. Every function here also takes an explicit ``threshold``, and the screen exposes it, because the appropriate cut depends on the assay.
records.label: spacr.confusion.confidence_threshold#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.context: Compare measurements across annotated gene groups and remaining cells.
records.label: spacr.gene_measurement_compare#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Compare measurements across annotated gene groups and remaining cells.
records.translation: Compare des mesures entre des groupes de gènes annotés et les cellules restantes.

records.context: Comparisons can use cells, microplate sample positions, or laboratory microplates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a microplate sample position; use the microplate sample position level when microplate sample positions are the experimental units.
records.label: spacr.gene_measurement_compare#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Comparisons can use cells, wells, or plates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a well; use the well level when wells are the experimental units.
records.translation: Les comparaisons peuvent utiliser des cellules, des puits ou des plaques comme observations. Le choix du test statistique est délégué à :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, et chaque résultat consigne ses éléments sur la normalité, l’égalité des variances et la taille d’échantillon. Les tests au niveau cellule traitent chaque cellule comme une observation et ne tiennent pas compte des cellules qui partagent un puits ; utilisez le niveau puits lorsque les puits sont les unités expérimentales.

records.translation: :func:`spacr.sp_stats.perform_statistical_tests` choisit entre le t-test de Student, le t-test de Welch, Mann-Whitney U, l’ANOVA à un facteur, l’ANOVA de Welch et Kruskal-Wallis selon le nombre de groupes et les vérifications d’hypothèses. records.source: Infer what the filenames in a folder of images encode, and import the folder.
records.translation: Déduit ce qu’encodent les noms de fichiers d’un dossier d’images, et importe le dossier.

records.context: A fixed list of filename conventions -- ``cellvoyager``, ``cq1``, ``custom`` (a user-written regular expression), ``auto`` -- covers few real layouts: of the ten acquisition layouts in ``tests/import_corpus.py``, two parse with it and eight recover nothing. Opera Phenix and ImageXpress are among the eight.
records.label: spacr.image_import#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A fixed list of filename conventions -- ``cellvoyager``, ``cq1``, ``custom`` (a user-written regular expression), ``auto`` -- covers few real layouts: of the ten acquisition layouts in ``tests/import_corpus.py``, two parse with it and eight recover nothing. Opera Phenix and ImageXpress are among the eight.
records.translation: Une liste fixe de conventions de nommage -- ``cellvoyager``, ``cq1``, ``custom`` (une expression régulière écrite par l’utilisateur), ``auto`` -- couvre peu de dispositions réelles : sur les dix dispositions d’acquisition de ``tests/import_corpus.py``, deux sont analysées avec elle et huit ne donnent rien. Opera Phenix et ImageXpress font partie des huit.

records.context: All ten layouts encode the same six facts -- laboratory microplate, microplate sample position, microscope field of view, channel, z, t -- and differ only in how. So rather than matching a whole filename against one of N templates, this module reads the parts of the name that vary across the folder and infers what each varying part means.
records.label: spacr.image_import#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: All ten layouts encode the same six facts -- plate, well, field, channel, z, t -- and differ only in how. So rather than matching a whole filename against one of N templates, this module reads the parts of the name that vary across the folder and infers what each varying part means.
records.translation: Les dix dispositions encodent toutes les six mêmes informations -- plaque, puits, champ, canal, z, t -- et ne diffèrent que par la manière. Plutôt que de confronter un nom de fichier entier à l’un de N modèles, ce module lit donc les parties du nom qui varient dans le dossier et déduit ce que signifie chaque partie variable.

records.context: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.label: spacr.image_import#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.translation: La variation à travers le dossier identifie les axes. Un jeton identique dans tous les fichiers ne porte aucune information : ``L01`` dans ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` est une constante pour toute la plaque et n’identifie rien. Un jeton qui prend deux valeurs sur huit fichiers est un axe à deux positions. Seul le dossier, et non un nom de fichier isolé, montre quels jetons sont des axes.

records.context: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.label: spacr.image_import#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.translation: Les marqueurs indiquent de quel axe relève un jeton variable. ``F001`` et ``C01`` varient tous deux et ne sont pas interchangeables ; la lettre placée devant nomme l’axe, et chaque convention du corpus en utilise une. La table des marqueurs ci-dessous constitue ce vocabulaire, et elle est courte parce que les conventions partagent pour la plupart leurs lettres.

records.context: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.label: spacr.image_import#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.translation: Aucun rôle n’est attribué sans preuve. Un jeton qui varie et ne porte aucun marqueur reconnaissable est signalé comme non placé, avec ses valeurs, afin que l’appelant puisse interroger l’utilisateur. Une arborescence partiellement impossible à analyser importe ce qu’elle peut et signale le reste, plutôt que de renvoyer une réponse plausible mais fausse ; l’ancien chemin ``consolidate`` perdait au contraire des images sans erreur.

records.context: ``context`` is a :class:`RegionContext` carrying the object type, the label mask, the ascending array of its non-zero label ids and (computed only if the hook asks for them) their centroids. records.source: ``context`` is a :class:`RegionContext` carrying the object type, the label mask, the ascending array of its non-zero label ids and (computed only if the hook asks for them) their centroids. The hook returns a boolean array of ``len(context.labels)``: ``True`` keeps the object, ``False`` drops it. Dropped labels are zeroed out of the mask *before* morphology or intensity is computed, so excluding 495 of 500 objects costs 5 objects' worth of work, not 500.
records.translation: ``context`` est un :class:`RegionContext` portant le type d’objet, le masque d’étiquettes, le tableau croissant de ses identifiants d’étiquettes non nuls et (calculés uniquement si le hook les demande) leurs centroïdes. Le hook renvoie un tableau booléen de longueur ``len(context.labels)`` : ``True`` conserve l’objet, ``False`` l’écarte. Les étiquettes écartées sont mises à zéro dans le masque *avant* le calcul de la morphologie ou de l’intensité, de sorte qu’exclure 495 objets sur 500 coûte le travail de 5 objets, et non de 500.

records.context: Preprocessing hooks form a **workflow**: each one receives the previous one's output. Order therefore matters, and ``priority`` is how two independent extensions agree on it without knowing about each other.

records.source: Preprocessing hooks form a **pipeline**: each one receives the previous one's output. Order therefore matters, and ``priority`` is how two independent extensions agree on it without knowing about each other.
records.translation: Les hooks de prétraitement forment un **pipeline** : chacun reçoit la sortie du précédent. L’ordre compte donc, et ``priority`` est le moyen par lequel deux extensions indépendantes s’accordent sur cet ordre sans se connaître.

records.context: Region filters **intersect**: every filter is handed the same, original set of labels, and an object is measured only if *every* filter kept it. records.source: A cell with four pathogens in it has four rows in ``pathogen`` and one in ``cell``. Putting a pathogen measurement on the same axis as a cell measurement means rolling those four up into one number -- and which number depends entirely on what is being measured:
records.translation: Une cellule contenant quatre pathogènes a quatre lignes dans ``pathogen`` et une dans ``cell``. Placer une mesure de pathogène sur le même axe qu’une mesure de cellule implique de réduire ces quatre valeurs à un seul nombre -- et ce nombre dépend entièrement de ce qui est mesuré :

records.context: area, perimeter, integrated intensity, counts   -> SUM minimum intensity                               -> MIN of the four maximum intensity                               -> MAX of the four mean, median                                    -> the object mean/median shape descriptors, positions                    -> mean text                                            -> the first
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: area, perimeter, integrated intensity, counts   -> SUM minimum intensity                               -> MIN of the four maximum intensity                               -> MAX of the four mean, median                                    -> the object mean/median shape descriptors, positions                    -> mean text                                            -> the first
records.translation: aire, périmètre, intensité intégrée, comptes   -> SUM intensité minimale                               -> MIN des quatre intensité maximale                               -> MAX des quatre moyenne, médiane                                    -> la moyenne/médiane de l’objet descripteurs de forme, positions                    -> moyenne texte                                            -> la première valeur

records.context: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse structured-data name and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse key and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.translation: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` effectue déjà cette jointure, et agrège chaque colonne numérique avec ``mean``. Cela répond en silence à une question différente pour chaque colonne : l’aire totale de quatre pathogènes devient une aire moyenne, un compte devient un compte moyen, et un minimum devient une moyenne de minima, qui n’est le minimum de rien. La jointure est par ailleurs saine -- c’est là que se trouvent le lien parent, la clé de timelapse et les vérifications de cardinalité --, si bien que ce module change la nature de l’agrégation, et non la manière dont les tables se retrouvent.

records.translation: Pour chaque colonne, les objets qui possèdent (HAVE) une valeur et ceux qui n’en ont pas sont comparés selon la distance entre leurs centroïdes dans la projection, exprimée en rayons de carte afin d’être comparable d’une exécution et d’une méthode à l’autre.

records.context: Measured on a synthetic infected/uninfected table with twelve pathogen columns, the median fill produced a centroid gap of 0.06 -- almost nothing -- and a dispersion ratio of 0.11. The centroid statistic alone would not have detected it, because a median fill puts the missing objects in the middle of the present ones rather than away from them. Both are reported, and ``severity`` is whichever is worse.
records.label: spacr.merge_tables.missingness_leak#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Measured on a synthetic infected/uninfected table with twelve pathogen columns, the median fill produced a centroid gap of 0.06 -- almost nothing -- and a dispersion ratio of 0.11. The centroid statistic alone would not have detected it, because a median fill puts the missing objects in the middle of the present ones rather than away from them. Both are reported, and ``severity`` is whichever is worse.
records.translation: Mesuré sur une table synthétique infectées/non infectées comportant douze colonnes de pathogène, le remplissage par la médiane a produit un écart de centroïdes de 0.06 -- presque rien -- et un rapport de dispersion de 0.11. La statistique de centroïdes seule ne l’aurait pas détecté, car un remplissage par la médiane place les objets manquants au milieu des objets présents plutôt qu’à l’écart. Les deux sont rapportés, et ``severity`` correspond au pire des deux.

records.translation: :mod:`spacr.artifacts` fournit la provenance et les vérifications d’obsolescence artefact par artefact : ``upstream_of`` / ``downstream_of`` parcourent les arêtes de provenance à partir d’un artefact, et ``is_stale`` indique si un artefact correspond encore à ce dont il a été fait. records.source: Two things are deliberately kept apart:
records.translation: Deux choses sont délibérément tenues séparées :

records.context: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.label: spacr.pipeline_graph#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.translation: **Obsolète n’est pas manquant.** Un artefact dont les entrées ont évolué est obsolète — le nombre qu’il contient ne découle plus des fichiers qu’il nomme. Un artefact supprimé est manquant — un problème de disponibilité. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` refuse déjà de les confondre, et ce module aussi : un nœud peut être les deux, et :attr:`Node.state` signale d’abord l’absence, car un fichier qui n’est pas là ne peut pas être relu pour vérifier quoi que ce soit d’autre.

records.context: **The registry is not the only source of truth.** A project can have run nothing at all, and a graph of zero nodes tells that user nothing. So :func:`module_graph` draws the *static* DAG from :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — what feeds what, by declaration — and :func:`build_graph` records which modules of it have actually produced something. The application view shows the module DAG behind the artifact DAG for exactly that reason: an empty project still gets a picture of the workflow it is about to execute.

records.source: **The registry is not the only source of truth.** A project can have run nothing at all, and a graph of zero nodes tells that user nothing. So :func:`module_graph` draws the *static* DAG from :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — what feeds what, by declaration — and :func:`build_graph` records which modules of it have actually produced something. The screen shows the module DAG behind the artifact DAG for exactly that reason: an empty project still gets a picture of the pipeline it is about to run.
records.translation: **Le registre n’est pas la seule source de vérité.** Un projet peut n’avoir rien exécuté du tout, et un graphe sans aucun nœud n’apprend rien à cet utilisateur. :func:`module_graph` dessine donc le DAG *statique* à partir de :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — ce qui alimente quoi, par déclaration — et :func:`build_graph` consigne lesquels de ses modules ont réellement produit quelque chose. L’écran montre le DAG des modules derrière le DAG des artefacts précisément pour cette raison : un projet vide obtient tout de même une image du pipeline qu’il s’apprête à exécuter.

records.context: A merge that silently changed how a measurement was combined produces a number that is wrong and looks fine, so :class:`PlateMerge` carries what the panel has to say: the anchor and the row count, the rows each source contributed, the measurements ``columns='common'`` dropped, the laboratory microplate ids shared across screens -- and every column that fell through to :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` because no rule matched it. records.source: A merge that silently changed how a measurement was combined produces a number that is wrong and looks fine, so :class:`PlateMerge` carries what the panel has to say: the anchor and the row count, the rows each source contributed, the measurements ``columns='common'`` dropped, the plate ids shared across screens -- and every column that fell through to :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` because no rule matched it. That last set is recomputed by re-walking ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`) rather than listed anywhere, so it cannot drift out of step with the rules.
records.translation: Une fusion qui modifierait en silence la manière de combiner une mesure produirait un nombre faux d’apparence correcte ; :class:`PlateMerge` porte donc ce que le panneau doit indiquer : l’ancre et le nombre de lignes, les lignes fournies par chaque source, les mesures écartées par ``columns='common'``, les identifiants de plaques partagés entre criblages -- et chaque colonne retombée sur :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` faute de règle correspondante. Ce dernier ensemble est recalculé en reparcourant ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`) plutôt que d’être listé quelque part, de sorte qu’il ne peut pas se désynchroniser des règles.

This module composes existing functions instead:

records.context: ``read_merged`` is *many databases, one table*. ``merge_tables`` is *one database, many tables* -- and it takes a PATH, so it cannot be handed a frame that has already been stacked across databases. This feature needs both, so the composition is: read each chosen table across every database, then roll the children onto the anchor.
records.label: spacr.plate_measurements#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``read_merged`` is *many databases, one table*. ``merge_tables`` is *one database, many tables* -- and it takes a PATH, so it cannot be handed a frame that has already been stacked across databases. This feature needs both, so the composition is: read each chosen table across every database, then roll the children onto the anchor.
records.translation: ``read_merged`` correspond à *plusieurs bases de données, une table*. ``merge_tables`` correspond à *une base de données, plusieurs tables* -- et prend un chemin (PATH) ; on ne peut donc pas lui transmettre un tableau déjà empilé à travers plusieurs bases de données. Cette fonctionnalité a besoin des deux, d’où la composition suivante : lire chaque table choisie dans toutes les bases de données, puis réduire les enfants sur l’ancre.

records.context: The module handles three issues:
records.label: spacr.profiler#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module handles three issues:
records.translation: Le module traite trois problèmes :

records.context: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a class label, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.label: spacr.profiler#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a CLASS LABEL, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.translation: **Les backends de régression prédisent différemment.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` couvre des résultats statsmodels (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, quatre familles GLM, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), des estimateurs scikit-learn (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) et l’ajusteur horseshoe. :func:`predict` est l’appel unique qui fonctionne sur tous, et :func:`response_scale` nomme ce qui a été renvoyé — car un GLM-binomial renvoie une probabilité, un Poisson GLM renvoie un taux, et ``LinearSVC.predict`` renvoie une étiquette de classe (CLASS LABEL), ce qui dessinerait une fonction en escalier ressemblant à un résultat. Le backend hinge est profilé via ``decision_function`` précisément pour cette raison, et l’échelle l’indique.

records.context: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.label: spacr.profiler#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.translation: **Rien ici ne réajuste.** Le modèle transmis est le modèle profilé. Un profileur qui réajuste discrètement montre à l’utilisateur un second modèle en l’étiquetant comme le premier, et sur un backend pénalisé avec ``alpha='auto'``, le second n’est même pas le même modèle. Lorsqu’un appelant ne dispose que des coefficients écrits et d’aucun objet vivant, :func:`from_coefficients` construit un :class:`FittedLinear` autour d’eux — cela revient à *lire* l’ajustement, non à le refaire, et la classe indique quelle fonction de lien elle applique.

records.context: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.label: spacr.profiler#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.translation: **Une valeur maintenue est un choix, pas une valeur par défaut.** :func:`reference_row` choisit la médiane de chaque colonne et l’indique explicitement ; l’argument ``at`` remplace n’importe laquelle d’entre elles ; et chaque :class:`Profile` porte le vecteur complet des valeurs maintenues, de sorte qu’une courbe peut toujours être rattachée aux hypothèses qui l’ont produite.

records.context: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (the ``hinge`` backend) has both that and ``predict``, and its ``predict`` returns a 0/1 CLASS. A profile of a class label is a step function, which reads as a finding and is an artefact of asking the wrong method. 2. a statsmodels results object — ``predict(exog)`` applies the inverse link, so a GLM comes back on the response scale. ``offset`` is passed when the object accepts one. 3. anything else with ``predict`` — the scikit-learn regressors. 4. the linear predictor from ``params`` / ``coef_``, for a fitted object that carries coefficients and nothing else (the horseshoe fitter).

records.source: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (the ``hinge`` backend) has both that and ``predict``, and its ``predict`` returns a 0/1 CLASS. A profile of a class label is a step function, which reads as a finding and is an artefact of asking the wrong method. 2. a statsmodels results object — ``predict(exog)`` applies the inverse link, so a GLM comes back on the response scale. ``offset`` is passed when the object accepts one. 3. anything else with ``predict`` — the scikit-learn regressors. 4. the linear predictor from ``params`` / ``coef_``, for a fitted object that carries coefficients and nothing else (the horseshoe fitter).
records.translation: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (le backend ``hinge``) possède à la fois cette méthode et ``predict``, et son ``predict`` renvoie une classe (CLASS) 0/1. Le profil d’une étiquette de classe est une fonction en escalier, qui se lit comme un résultat et n’est qu’un artefact dû au choix de la mauvaise méthode. 2. un objet de résultats statsmodels — ``predict(exog)`` applique la fonction de lien inverse, de sorte qu’un GLM revient sur l’échelle de la réponse. ``offset`` est transmis lorsque l’objet en accepte un. 3. tout autre objet doté de ``predict`` — les régresseurs scikit-learn. 4. le prédicteur linéaire issu de ``params`` / ``coef_``, pour un objet ajusté qui porte des coefficients et rien d’autre (l’ajusteur horseshoe).
